title: Georgia's 7th Congressional District General Election, 2026
description: The 2026 general election for Georgia's 7th Congressional District pits incumbent Republican Rep. Rich McCormick against the Democratic nominee following a June 16 primary runoff between Tony Kozycki and Case Norton. The district, redrawn by a court-ordered round of redistricting, now covers most of the northern metro Atlanta area including all of Dawson, Forsyth, and Lumpkin counties. Once a competitive swing seat, the district has shifted to the right in recent cycles, with Donald Trump carrying it by 22 points in the 2024 presidential election. The race centers on national issues such as healthcare costs, government spending, immigration, and trust in government, with both Democratic candidates emphasizing working-class economic concerns.

candidates.name: Rich McCormick
candidates.summary: Rich McCormick is a decorated U.S. Marine Corps and Navy veteran, an emergency room physician, and the incumbent U.S. Representative for Georgia's 7th Congressional District. First elected to represent Georgia's 6th District in 2022 and then elected to the 7th District in 2024, he serves on the House Armed Services, Oversight, and Science, Space, and Technology Committees. McCormick emphasizes conservative positions on border security, fiscal responsibility, and national defense, and has been a vocal critic of federal spending on entitlement programs.

candidates.name: Tony Kozycki
candidates.summary: Tony Kozycki is a Navy combat veteran and immigration attorney running for Congress in Georgia's 7th District. A graduate of the U.S. Naval Academy, he served as a Naval Aviator flying F/A-18 Super Hornets on three combat deployments and was awarded three Air Medals. After his military service, he earned a Juris Doctor from Georgia State University College of Law summa cum laude and has practiced as an attorney focused on immigration and criminal defense. Kozycki's campaign emphasizes affordability, healthcare reform, government accountability, and a secure border paired with a functional immigration system.

candidates.name: Case Norton
candidates.summary: Case Norton is a union camera technician and working-class progressive candidate running for Congress in Georgia's 7th District. A member of IATSE Local 600 with 19 years of experience in the film industry as a 1st AC (first assistant camera), Norton moved from Los Angeles to Sandy Springs, Georgia. His campaign focuses on Medicare for All, codifying Roe v. Wade, increasing housing supply, banning congressional stock trading, and reducing corporate influence in politics. He has been endorsed by progressive and labor organizations and emphasizes his experience as a working-class father navigating the same economic pressures as his constituents.

forecast.rationale: No district-level polling exists for this race, which caps confidence and prevents a safe rating. However, the structural signals are strongly Republican: McCormick is the incumbent in a redrawn district that Trump carried by 22 points in 2024, the district has shifted right from its earlier competitive status, and the Democratic nominee (winner of the June 16 runoff between Kozycki and Norton) has yet to consolidate and faces a well-funded incumbent in a Republican-leaning midterm environment. The Trump+22 baseline and incumbency together point to a clear Republican advantage in the 80-94% range, consistent with a likely-r rating. The 17-point margin estimate reflects the Trump+22 baseline tempered by the uncertainty of a newly configured district and the absence of direct survey evidence.
